channel.title: THD美籍华人英语访谈秀
channel.description: The Honest Drink是一个每周更新的英语访谈节目，由三位在中国的美籍华人主持。我们讨论自我完善、社会、东西方文化和生活方式等话题。我们经常有专家嘉宾来参加我们的节目，聆听他们的经验和想法。当然，我们每集都喝好酒! 我的酒馆对你不打烊... Three American-raised friends in China candidly explore issues on current culture, self-help, society, nationality and the madness of modern behavior. They drink with special guests as they make attempts at self-improvement, reducing misconceptions about the world and ourselves, stumbling their way towards becoming happier, healthier and wiser.

item.title: #199- Rachel & Timothee: Off The Menu
item.description:
Rachel Gouk is the creator of the popular Shanghai food blog Nomfluence.  She is also the founder of Shanghai Burger Month and a consultant for F&B brands.  Timothee Becqueriaux is an accomplished mixologist and bartender, currently spearheading the cocktail program at Bar Mixato.  He is also a winner of the global Chivas Masters cocktail competition.  Today we talk about food, taste and love.  We compare dining standards between Europe and Shanghai, and debate “authenticity” versus personal memory in taste. We dissect how awards and ratings (Michelin, 50 Best, Dianping) are gamified, and float the idea of “food Tinder”.  We discuss cultural differences in communal versus individual dining, how palates evolve (bitterness, spice), favorite comfort foods, curry preferences, cooking at home, and the thin margins and pressures of running F&B.  We also talk about Rachel and Timothee’s relationship as a romantic couple and how food plays a central role keeping them together despite there differences.  This is a wild one where we go off-script and off-menu.

item.title: #198- Lee Mack: The Carrot or the Stick
item.description:
Lee Mack is an education innovator, investor and researcher.  He is co-founder of Meridian Education and also writes a newsletter called Educationology.  He was previously Director of Admissions and Marketing at Wellington College International Shanghai.  Today, we discuss the enormous and innovative changes that need to happen both inside and outside our schools.  We discuss the debate around Wang Hong’s comments after winning the Fields Medal and compare Chinese and American approaches to schooling, including academic pressure, student autonomy, family expectations, and the purpose of an education.  We talk about new education pathways, homeschooling and what children still need to learn for themselves when AI can supply all the answers.

item.title: #197- David Ammerschlaeger: Artificially Human
item.description:
David Ammerschlaeger is a clinical psychologist and Chief psychological counselor at ChingHo Medical Clinic in Shanghai. Today we talk about whether humanity will be ok.  We discuss AI, digital technology and their effects on people’s thinking and relationships.  We talk about the “validation vortex”, learned ADHD, and consciousness.  We also talk about AI companions, sex-bots, and the hyper-sexualization of society.  We discuss the dire consequences of outsourcing our decision-making to technology, the difficulty so many people are having with intimate relationships, and not losing connection to nature, ourselves, and each other.

item.title: #196- Yaling Jiang: Through Chinese Eyes
item.description:
Yaling Jiang is a writer and researcher helping people understand China through real individuals, rather than through headlines or stereotypes.  Yaling is a former journalist and translator and founder of the popular newsletter Following the Yuan.  She is also the founder of the research and strategy consultancy ApertureChina.  Today, Yaling joins us to talk about what it really means to explain China to the outside world—and why seeing Chinese people as individuals matters.  We talk about what it’s like to have your country, your culture, and your own identity be misunderstood.  We also talk about the growing desire among Chinese women to have more control over the lives they choose to live.  We talk about dating, marriage, motherhood, gender expectations and the fear of becoming “leftover”.  We explore how younger generations are challenging traditional norms and whether China’s changing social attitudes are pointing toward a more equal future.  We also talk about the loneliness of a world that feels increasingly divided, and Yaling’s hope that we can learn to see each other as individuals rather than stereotypes. It’s a conversation about identity, agency, belonging—and the fragile hope that we might find our way back to each other.

item.title: #195- Mike Pistilli: A Positive Influence
item.description:
Mike Pistilli (麦霹雳) is a fitness professional, social-media influencer, mental health advocate and NASM Certified Personal Trainer. He is known on Chinese platforms as 麦霹雳 or Coach Mike. Having worked across Chinese and Western fitness cultures, Mike brings a practical, positive and unusually candid perspective to health, body image and online influence. Today we talk about China's changing culture around fitness, social media personalities and society.  We talk about why fitness has become a new status symbol, and how social-media rules shape what creators can responsibly share. We also discuss happiness and Mike's new VR fitness and mental-health project, FunFitland. Mike explains how his own experience of growing up insecure shaped his coaching philosophy, and why his personal rule is to leave people feeling more positive than when he met them.

item.title: #193- Zak Dychtwald: Cut Throat
item.description:
Zak Dychtwald is the founder and CEO of BridgeWorks Global and author of the critically acclaimed book, Young China.  He runs a cross-geography collaboration lab, helping people in some of the world’s largest companies get along better across national borders, through science and data backed research.  Zak is a distinguished speaker having delivered over 100 keynotes to Fortune 500 companies and global investor. Today we talk about the brutal side of competition and collaboration between people, society, business and countries.  Zak explains why he founded BridgeWorks and outlines the seven factors preventing effective global collaboration between working people.  We compare work culture between Chinese companies and the rest of the world and explore China’s internal competitive intensity, education pressures and scarcity mindset.  We also talk about AI’s impact on jobs and what a life is for.

item.title: #192 Cyrus Janssen: It's Not All Scary
item.description:
Cyrus Janssen is a YouTuber and speaker on China and the world.  Today we talk about countering fear-driven narratives about other countries, being a “global citizen”, and its impact on how we engage or disengage with the rest of the world.  We also talk about Chinese brands in America, as cost-of-living pressures rise and US domestic polarization and war continues.  Cyrus also describes how he was recently offered $10,000 US dollars to lie to his viewers, and how the money was ultimately traced back to perhaps the most recognizable AI company in the world.

item.title: #191 Julie Sun: Love Practically
item.description:
Julie Sun is a brand marketer and content creator who creates English content on Instagram and TikTok as, “Julie your China friend”, explaining Chinese culture and dating to foreigners.  Having worked in international marketing across the world, her sociological research has brought her traveling to over 30 countries, often by herself.  Now she uses her voice to introduce modern China to a Western audience, providing an honest perspective on Chinese society, dating and everyday life.  Today we talk about modern society and the search for our place in it.  We talk about when after receiving countless messages from foreign men asking her to help them find a Chinese wife, Julie found herself researching China's matchmaking industry—and what she discovered raised difficult questions about love, practicality, immigration, family expectations, and whether the search for the "perfect partner" has become one of the defining struggles of our generation.  We talk about differences between Western and Chinese communication styles, criticism and social norms around hugging, staying friends with exes, and saying “I love you”.  We also get into marriage customs like cai li or dowry, financial independence, and the quarter-life crisis.

item.title: #190- Eric Hovagim: The New American Dream
item.description:
Eric Hovagim is an American content producer, industrial engineer and political commentator who, in his own words, moved to China in late 2025 to escape "the American Century of Humiliation”.  He worked in New York City, producing a handful of videos that helped get Zohran Mamdani elected mayor in 2025.  Recently, Eric has been producing content for popular commentator, Hasan Piker.  He was previously also part of a climate-policy think tank in the US and an engineer on the Hyperloop team.  Today, we talk about why Eric is here in China and what he hopes to learn.  He shares his frustrations with the state of affairs in the US and the crisis of the American dream.  He argues the need for revolutionary change and optimism as we talk about what he’s observing in China that he could one day bring back to America.  We also talk about societal fear, AI concerns, Eric’s self-identification as a socialist and what annoys him about being here.  We share plenty of laughs in an otherwise serious discussion, and we might also have offended all French people.

item.title: #189- Raffe, BT & Dino: To Live and Die in Shanghai pt.2
item.description:
Raffe is the owner of Cantina Agave,  the very first Mexican restaurant in Shanghai.  Today he is joined by some old friends, BT and Dino on the podcast, as we celebrate Cantina’s 18th anniversary and the launch of his new restaurant, Vice.  We talk about why he’s stayed in Shanghai and discuss the constant pressure to keep up with this unique city, the challenges of running F&B amid unpredictable rules and high turnover, and how the city shifted from “wild east” days to stricter, safer, more equal enforcement.  We compare Shanghai’s convenience and safety with rising costs, crime, and lenient enforcement in the U.S., especially LA, and talk about perspective, media-driven fear, and cultural adaptation. We talk about a renaissance in Shanghai’s dining scene, social media’s impact, and Cantina’s clientele flipping to 70% local Chinese. We also end the episode with a blindfolded taco taste test that doesn’t go as planned.

item.title: #187- YI: The Love Bomb
item.description:
YI is the owner of fine jewelry brand YI Collection and former stylist for Vogue China.  Today we talk about “love bombing”, attraction, sex and the city…literally.  We talk about the differences in what men and women might be attracted to and the games we play when we’re in the chase.  We talk about rejection, self-worth, appearance vs personality, and judging faces.  YI shares her mindset after leaving a relationship of eight years, her views on independence, loneliness, monogamy, white expat men, and dating strategies like negging and acting dumb. We discuss ethnicity and identity as Chinese-Americans, changing beauty standards, and the importance of health and fitness in maintaining marriages and relationships.  We also talk about squat toilets.

item.title: #186- Dr. Steve Vinay Gunther: The Truth About Us
item.description:
Dr. Steve Vinay Gunther is a renowned Australian Gestalt psychotherapist and founder of the acclaimed Northern Rivers Gestalt Institute in Australia.  He is also the author of the bestselling book “The Woman In Your Life - A Man’s Guide to a Happy Relationship”.  He has been in practice for over 40 years with an accomplished career in psychology, working with individuals, couples and families from all over the world.  

Today, Dr. Gunther shares why his focus shifted to China and we get into a deep conversation about relationships.  We talk about what prevents us from sustaining healthy relationships and when to walk away.  We cover failed marriages, self-awareness, listening for “grains of truth” and men’s difficulty identifying and expressing deeper feelings.   We talk about shame, “un-virtues” and why running away from pain doesn’t work.  We also discuss the over-simplification of therapy in this digital age, the dangers of using AI for emotional guidance, and a wholistic way of perceiving our own existence called systems thinking.  We explore relationships from at least three levels, the relationship with ourselves, the ones we love, and society.  Join us as we uncover some hard truths.

item.title: #185- Matt Chen: A Chinese Time In My Life
item.description:
Matt Chen is a Chinese American entrepreneur, social media content creator, and builder of Daily Hanzi, an app helping people learn to read Chinese.  Currently at 24 years old he’s decided to ditch his aerospace engineering degree and restart his life by moving to China.  Focused on bridging East and West through content about language, culture and identity he hopes to reconnect with his Asian heritage while improving his own Chinese literacy, finding a different path for himself in a new world.  Today, we talk about Matt’s experience growing up in the US as an ABC and compare it to our own experience from an older generation.  We talk about his choice to move to China just ten months ago, his revelation during a job interview with a US defense contractor, and what’s behind the “A Very Chinese Time In My Life” trend happening in America.  We also talk about the broad anxiety amongst his younger generation, finding purpose, and balancing digital and analog life.  

Happy Chinese New Year!

item.description:
We are joined by friends of the show Charles Zeng, owner of Charlie’s Burger, and James Wu visiting from the U.S.  Today we debate the pros and cons of having kids or not.  James shares his reasoning on his and his wife’s decision not to have kids.  We talk about societal pressures, its impact on marriage and our thoughts on using physical force when it comes to disciplining our kids.  We talk about chasing happiness, comparing kids to chocolate, and our biggest fears when it comes to growing old.  We talk about the midlife crisis, aging and managing anger day to day.
